title: GraphRAG
shortDefinition: An enhancement to RAG that uses a knowledge graph to retrieve connected information across documents, not just similar passages.
definition: GraphRAG is an enhancement to standard RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) that builds a knowledge graph over source documents, allowing retrieval to follow explicit entity relationships and connections across documents — rather than only retrieving passages whose embedding vectors are numerically similar to the query's embedding. Where standard RAG retrieves isolated passages, GraphRAG can retrieve connected chains of related information: 'what companies are connected to this acquisition?' retrieves a graph traversal across documents, not just the most similar individual passages.

sections.title: Why standard RAG misses relationship-dependent questions
sections.description: Vector similarity works for single passages but fails for questions requiring connections across documents.

content.text: Standard vector similarity retrieval works well for questions answered by a single passage or a few similar passages — 'what is the return policy?' retrieves the relevant passage. It struggles with questions that require connecting information distributed across many documents in ways that aren't captured by any single passage's similarity to the query: 'which of our customers are exposed to this supplier's regulatory risk?' requires traversing a graph of customer-supplier-regulatory relationships that no individual document passage captures in a retrievable form. GraphRAG builds this relationship structure explicitly, making it queryable in ways vector search alone cannot support.

Example — customer-supplier-regulatory risk relationships.

content.title: The key insight
content.text: Standard RAG retrieves similar passages. GraphRAG traverses connected relationships — solving a fundamentally different class of questions.

sections.title: When GraphRAG is worth the added complexity

content.text: GraphRAG adds substantial complexity to RAG architecture — building and maintaining the knowledge graph over source documents is a significant additional engineering investment compared to standard vector indexing. It's most clearly justified for knowledge bases where relationship traversal questions are central use cases: enterprise knowledge about organizational structures, customer-supplier-product relationships, regulatory entity connections, or research literature where citation and concept relationships carry meaning that passage similarity doesn't capture. For simpler question-answering over documents where most questions are answered by a single relevant passage, standard RAG delivers most of the value at a fraction of the complexity.

items: Substantial complexity — beyond standard RAG implementation.
Justified when — relationship traversal is a central use case.
Enterprise org structures — customer-supplier-product relationships.
Regulatory connections — entity relationship mapping.
Research literature — citation and concept relationships.

items: "How much will this cost?" — $20,000–$220,000 depending on whether this is a feasibility assessment or a full implementation. Fixed quote after Discovery.

"Should we use GraphRAG or standard RAG for our use case?" — ClickMasters assesses this honestly during Discovery — most question-answering use cases are adequately served by well-tuned standard RAG; GraphRAG is most clearly justified when relationship traversal across documents is a primary, repeated question type.

"Does GraphRAG always produce better answers than standard RAG?" — Not universally — for simple passage-retrieval questions, standard RAG often performs equivalently at much lower complexity. GraphRAG's advantage is specific to relationship-dependent queries that span multiple documents in ways vector similarity can't capture.

"How is GraphRAG different from standard RAG?" — Standard RAG retrieves passages by vector similarity; GraphRAG additionally builds a knowledge graph over documents, enabling retrieval by traversing explicit entity relationships.

content.text: GraphRAG has limitations. It adds significant implementation complexity and cost compared to standard RAG. The knowledge graph extraction pipeline can be error-prone, especially for unstructured documents. GraphRAG requires ongoing maintenance as documents are updated. It may not improve performance on simple passage-retrieval questions. The graph structure may not capture all relevant relationships, and the hybrid retrieval system adds latency. GraphRAG is not a replacement for standard RAG — it addresses a specific class of questions at higher cost.

items.question: Who developed GraphRAG?
items.answer: Microsoft Research published influential work on GraphRAG in 2024, though the concept of combining knowledge graphs with RAG had earlier precedents; ClickMasters implements GraphRAG drawing on both research advances and practical production experience.

items.question: How is GraphRAG different from standard RAG?
items.answer: Standard RAG retrieves passages by vector similarity; GraphRAG additionally builds a knowledge graph over documents, enabling retrieval by traversing explicit entity relationships — better suited to questions spanning connected information across many documents.

items.question: Does GraphRAG require a separate knowledge graph database?
items.answer: Yes, the knowledge graph is stored in a graph database (like Neo4j) alongside the vector store; ClickMasters selects appropriate infrastructure based on your existing stack and scale requirements.

items.question: How is the knowledge graph built from source documents?
items.answer: Through entity extraction and relationship identification from document content — ClickMasters builds this extraction pipeline using NLP and LLM-assisted techniques tuned to your specific document types and entity vocabulary.

items.question: How long does a GraphRAG implementation take?
items.answer: 14–32 weeks for full implementation, considerably longer than standard RAG given the added knowledge graph construction and hybrid retrieval complexity.

items.question: Can GraphRAG and standard RAG be combined in the same system?
items.answer: Yes, hybrid systems that route queries to graph traversal or vector retrieval based on query type are common — ClickMasters designs the routing logic based on your specific question type distribution.

items.question: What is the relationship between GraphRAG and knowledge graphs?
items.answer: GraphRAG uses a knowledge graph as the retrieval structure. The knowledge graph stores entities and relationships extracted from documents; GraphRAG traverses this graph to retrieve connected information for answering queries.

items.question: Does GraphRAG require more computational resources than standard RAG?
items.answer: Yes — GraphRAG requires additional infrastructure for the knowledge graph database, extraction pipeline, and hybrid retrieval. The incremental cost should be weighed against the improvement in relationship-dependent question answering.

items.question: What types of documents are best suited for GraphRAG?
items.answer: GraphRAG is most valuable for documents with rich entity relationships — organizational charts, regulatory filings, supply chain documents, research literature with citation networks, and any content where connections between entities carry meaning.

items.question: Can GraphRAG be implemented incrementally?
items.answer: Yes — you can start with a single knowledge domain or a subset of documents, validate the approach, and expand coverage. ClickMasters recommends this phased approach for managing complexity.
